group-index.text: x sub i j is observation j in group i. There are c groups, n_i observations per group and n observations in total.
group-index.title: Group Index

one-model.text: An observation equals its group population mean plus an independent normal error with mean zero and common variance sigma squared.
one-model.title: One Model

one-means.text: The group mean averages that group. The overall sample mean weights each group mean by its sample size.
one-means.title: One Means

equal-target.text: An equal-level population average gives each group equal weight; its effects sum to zero. Average the group sample means equally to estimate it.
equal-target.title: Equal Target

weighted-target.text: With fixed group sample sizes, the grand sample mean estimates the sample-size-weighted population mean, not generally the equal-level mean.
weighted-target.title: Weighted Target

one-ss.text: Total squared deviations from the grand mean equal between-group squared deviations plus within-group squared deviations.
one-ss.title: One Ss

one-proof.tex: \begin{aligned}x_{ij}-\bar x&=(x_{ij}-\bar x_i)+(\bar x_i-\bar x),\\\sum_j(x_{ij}-\bar x_i)&=0,\\\sum_i\sum_j2(x_{ij}-\bar x_i)(\bar x_i-\bar x)&=0.\end{aligned}
one-proof.text: Decompose each deviation into a within-group residual and a group-mean deviation. The cross-product sums to zero because residuals within each group sum to zero.
one-proof.title: One Proof

one-null.tex: H_0:\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_c,\qquad H_1:\text{not all population means are equal}
one-null.text: The null says all group population means are equal. The alternative says at least one differs, not that all differ.
one-null.title: One Null

one-f.text: Divide between and within sums of squares by their degrees of freedom. Under the null and classical assumptions, their ratio follows an F distribution.
one-f.title: One F

one-p.text: The p-value is the upper-tail probability beyond the observed F statistic. Compare it with alpha, or compare observed F with the lower-tail 1 minus alpha quantile.
one-p.title: One P

chisquares.text: Within-group sum of squares divided by the error variance has n minus c chi-square degrees of freedom. Under the equal-means null, the between-group version has c minus 1 degrees of freedom. They are independent.
chisquares.title: Chisquares

expected-ms.text: Within-group mean square estimates the common error variance under both hypotheses. Between-group mean square adds a nonnegative population mean-separation term.
expected-ms.title: Expected Ms

f-t.text: With two groups, between-group sum of squares reduces to the squared difference scaled by group sizes, and ANOVA F equals the squared pooled t statistic.
f-t.title: F T

effect-size.text: Eta squared is the sample fraction of total variation explained by groups. Omega squared subtracts a degrees-of-freedom correction and uses an adjusted denominator.
effect-size.title: Effect Size

two-index.text: An observation has factor A level i, factor B level j and replicate k. Balanced replication means m observations in every one of c times r cells.
two-index.title: Two Index

two-model.text: Each observation equals a grand mean, factor A effect, factor B effect, interaction effect and independent normal error with common variance.
two-model.title: Two Model

two-pop-means.text: The grand mean is the equal average of all cell population means. The A marginal mean averages across B levels; the B marginal mean averages across A levels.
two-pop-means.title: Two Pop Means

two-effects.text: Main effects are marginal means minus the grand mean. The interaction is the cell mean minus both marginal means plus the grand mean.
two-effects.title: Two Effects

two-constraints.text: Main effects sum to zero. Interaction effects sum to zero down each column and across each row, not merely across the entire table.
two-constraints.title: Two Constraints

two-sample-means.text: The sample grand mean averages all observations; a cell mean averages its m replicates; each marginal mean averages all observations at that factor level.
two-sample-means.title: Two Sample Means

two-estimates.tex: \hat\mu=\bar x,\quad \hat\alpha_i=\bar x_{i\cdot}-\bar x,\quad \hat\beta_j=\bar x_{\cdot j}-\bar x,\quad \hat\tau_{ij}=\bar x_{ij}-\bar x_{i\cdot}-\bar x_{\cdot j}+\bar x
two-estimates.text: Estimate the grand mean and effects by replacing population means with their sample counterparts.
two-estimates.title: Two Estimates

two-expectations.text: Expectations of the sample means equal the corresponding grand, marginal and cell population means.
two-expectations.title: Two Expectations

two-ss.tex: \begin{aligned}\mathrm{SSA}&=rm\sum_i(\bar x_{i\cdot}-\bar x)^2\\\mathrm{SSB}&=cm\sum_j(\bar x_{\cdot j}-\bar x)^2\\\mathrm{SSAB}&=m\sum_i\sum_j(\bar x_{ij}-\bar x_{i\cdot}-\bar x_{\cdot j}+\bar x)^2\\\mathrm{SSE}&=\sum_i\sum_j\sum_k(x_{ijk}-\bar x_{ij})^2\\\mathrm{SST}&=\mathrm{SSA}+\mathrm{SSB}+\mathrm{SSAB}+\mathrm{SSE}.\end{aligned}
two-ss.text: Balanced two-way total variation splits into A marginal variation, B marginal variation, interaction variation and residual variation within cells.
two-ss.title: Two Ss

two-deviation.tex: x_{ijk}-\bar x=(\bar x_{i\cdot}-\bar x)+(\bar x_{\cdot j}-\bar x)+(\bar x_{ij}-\bar x_{i\cdot}-\bar x_{\cdot j}+\bar x)+(x_{ijk}-\bar x_{ij})
two-deviation.text: A total deviation splits into an A effect, B effect, interaction and within-cell residual.
two-deviation.title: Two Deviation

two-tests.text: Test whether all A effects are zero, all B effects are zero, or all interactions are zero. Each divides its mean square by the common within-cell error mean square.
two-tests.title: Two Tests

two-ems.text: For a balanced fixed-effects model, each effect mean square contains error variance plus its squared population effect contribution; the error mean square contains only the error variance.
two-ems.title: Two Ems

depth-weighted-means.title: Two averages for unequal group counts
depth-weighted-means.text: The sample grand mean weights the three means by 2, 4 and 6 orders, giving 24 and five sixths minutes. The equal-process average is 23 and two thirds minutes.

depth-weighted-effects.title: Count-weighted effects cancel
depth-weighted-effects.text: The count-weighted deviations of group means from the sample grand mean sum to zero: 2 times negative 29 over 6, plus 4 times negative 5 over 6, plus 6 times 13 over 6.

depth-interaction-constraints.title: One independent interaction in a two-by-two design
depth-interaction-constraints.text: With offers in rows and day types in columns, the interaction entries are d, negative d, negative d and d. Every row and every column sums to zero, leaving one free interaction value.
